Architectural Principles of Modern Distributed Systems
Distributed systems require careful decoupling between storage and computation to achieve high throughput and predictable latency.
Eventual consistency allows decentralized nodes to process reads and writes locally without blocking for global consensus across network partitions.
Observability platforms must aggregate telemetry metrics, distributed traces, and structured logs to maintain operational reliability.

Core Runtime Architecture and Execution Model
The runtime schedules lightweight tasks across a pool of worker threads using lock-free work-stealing queues.
Memory safety is enforced through static lifetime analysis and ownership semantics without requiring garbage collection pauses.
Asynchronous input and output operations leverage native platform event loops to minimize operating system context switches.
